About Priva 

In the middle of Het Westland, where innovation in food and flowers has been thriving for decades, Priva builds technology that keeps greenhouses growing and buildings breathing. We create intelligent control systems that help customers operate sustainable, reliable environments.

Why this role matters 

Our platform capabilities span multiple services and teams. Individual components can pass their own tests while a customer journey still fails at an interface, in shared data, during deployment or under realistic operating conditions. This role closes that gap.

Establish a coherent end-to-end quality approach across the platform capabilities owned by Teams Mobius and Rangers.
Unify and improve existing integration and system-level test approaches instead of creating another isolated test suite.
Give product teams practical tooling and guidance so their components can participate in complete platform journeys.
Turn production risks, incidents and cross-team dependencies into repeatable tests and stronger release evidence.

Your teams 

You will work across Team Mobius and Team Rangers. Mobius owns data-platform capabilities, including master and historical data services. Rangers owns cloud services including remote data communication. You will collaborate closely with engineers, QA colleagues, Product, architects, application teams and support specialists.

What you'll do 

Create and maintain a platform-level end-to-end test strategy covering critical customer and operational journeys across services.
Map system boundaries, dependencies, data flows and failure modes, then translate the highest risks into executable test scenarios.
Build and maintain automated tests that exercise real service interfaces and representative environments.
Bring existing team-level test frameworks and suites into a coherent approach, reusing what works and removing unnecessary duplication.
Define test data, environment, identity and dependency-management patterns that make cross-service tests repeatable and diagnosable.
Integrate smoke, regression and end-to-end suites into CI/CD pipelines with useful reporting and clear ownership of failures.
Coordinate cross-team test preparation for changes that affect multiple services, consumers or production environments.
Use telemetry, logs, traces and test evidence to diagnose failures and distinguish product defects from environment or data issues.
Assess release risk, communicate residual risk clearly and help teams make evidence-based release decisions.
Coach engineers and QA colleagues in testability, system-level thinking and effective automation.

Essentials 

Professional experience in integration, system or end-to-end testing of distributed software systems.
Strong test-automation skills and the ability to create maintainable frameworks, libraries and workflows rather than only individual test cases.
Programming or scripting ability in at least one language commonly used for test automation, such as C#, Python, TypeScript or PowerShell.
Experience testing REST APIs, asynchronous integrations, data flows and service-to-service authentication.
Practical CI/CD experience, including automated test execution, result publishing and failure investigation.
Working knowledge of cloud environments, containers, networking, configuration and observability.
Ability to reason across team and service boundaries, identify hidden dependencies and focus effort on the highest operational risks.
A collaborative approach: you enable teams to own quality rather than becoming a final testing gate.
Clear communication, documentation and stakeholder alignment skills.

Useful additional experience 

Microsoft Azure services and Azure DevOps or GitHub-based delivery workflows.
Playwright, Reqnroll or SpecFlow, Robot Framework, Pytest, Pester, xUnit or comparable tooling.
SQL, data-platform testing, multi-tenant systems or historical time-series data.
IoT Edge, gateways, MQTT, remote device communication or mixed cloud and edge solutions.
Performance, resilience, security or compatibility testing of distributed systems.
Building automation, horticulture, operational technology or other systems with physical-world dependencies.

Why choose Eneco?

At Eneco we work towards one clear goal: being fully climate neutral by 2035. Homes are a big part of that. More and more people generate their own power, store it in a battery and charge a car at home.

Our Home Energy Management platform ties all of that together and steers it, so energy is used when it is greenest and cheapest. That platform is growing fast and connects to the wider Eneco ecosystem. Scaling it brings the kind of engineering challenges you want: many devices, many integrations, high reliability demands.

You take complex features and integrations from refinement all the way to production, independently.
You turn architecture designs into practical solutions that stay scalable and easy to maintain.
You build event-driven services and APIs that connect devices in and around the home.
You automate infrastructure and deployments with Terraform (Infrastructure as Code) and CI/CD pipelines.
You dig into cross-service and production issues and fix the root cause, not just the symptom.
You spot gaps in a design, technical risks and dependencies early, and raise them before they become problems.
You lift the team through code reviews, pairing and knowledge sharing.

Is this about you?

You have several years of experience building and running cloud services at scale, ideally on Azure. Strong AWS or GCP experience translates well.

You are comfortable with Terraform and CI/CD, and you take testing, security, observability and reliability seriously.
You own what you build, communicate clearly with engineers and non-engineers, and deliver predictably.

The technical growth of the people around you, through reviews, pairing and clear documentation.

This is where you’ll work

You join an engineering team that likes good software but stays pragmatic. Everyone owns their work end to end, and as a senior you help shape the architecture instead of only receiving it. You work closely with fellow engineers, architects and product, and there is plenty of room to bring in your own ideas.

Job Description:
We’re an independent AA studio founded by two brothers with a dream; inspired by games like Anarchy Online, Star Wars Galaxies, Neocron and WoW, we’re pushing the bounds of the genre with polished gameplay, vibrant visuals, and a dash of creative ideas never seen before.
With a passion for immersive world building, our fast-growing team of multi-national talent is using Unreal Engine 5 to build a revolutionary MMORPG that blends traditional philosophies with trailblazing innovation.
Our studio in Weesp is easily accessible by public transport (station Weesp) and car (A1), and offers an environment where positive work culture stands central to effective collaboration.
Working in-house at Grid Games means an opportunity to directly shape the evolution of our ambitious vision.

WE’RE LOOKING FOR
We’re looking for an IT / DevOps Engineer to join our growing engineering/devops team.
This is a hands-on role with an approximately 50/50 split between DevOps/Build Engineering and internal IT/System Administration. You’ll help build and maintain the infrastructure that our developers rely on every day, while also taking ownership of the studio’s internal IT environment.
You’ll work closely with developers and other engineers to automate processes, improve development workflows and keep our infrastructure secure, reliable and scalable.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

DevOps & Build Engineering
Build, maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines and automated development workflows.
Work with Unreal Engine build and pipeline systems, including Horde.
Maintain and improve build infrastructure, with a focus on reliability and developer experience.
Automate infrastructure and repetitive processes using scripting and Infrastructure as Code.
Help design, deploy and maintain backend and development infrastructure.
Monitor systems and proactively improve reliability, performance and security.

IT & Systems Administration
Own the studio’s day-to-day IT infrastructure, including hardware, servers, accounts and internal services.
Own workspace IT by setting up workspaces and keeping them maintained.
Administer Microsoft 365, Azure, Active Directory and Group Policy.
Manage Windows and Linux systems and our virtualisation environment.
Maintain networking infrastructure, including DNS, DHCP, subnets, IP ranges and routing.
Maintain network cabling and switches, access points, server room, meeting room AV, etc.
Implement and maintain backup, disaster recovery and security measures.
Manage software licensing across the studio. Provisioning new accounts, managing renewals and generating cost reports.
Maintain an inventory of our IT assets, and budget the hardware refresh cycle.
Manage imaging and deployment, patching, security and disk encryption.
Provide hands-on IT support to the team when needed.

YOUR QUALIFICATIONS
HBO/Bachelor-level working and thinking ability, or equivalent practical experience.
4+ years of relevant professional experience.
Experience administering Windows and Linux environments.
Strong understanding of networking fundamentals: DNS, DHCP, subnets, IP ranges and routing.
Experience with Active Directory, Group Policy and Microsoft 365 and/or Azure.
Experience building or maintaining CI/CD pipelines.
Experience with scripting or automation using PowerShell, Bash, Python or a similar language.
Experience with source control systems such as Perforce, Git or SVN.
A strong security mindset and experience with backups and disaster recovery.
Able to work independently, take ownership and see systems through from implementation to maintenance.
Comfortable collaborating closely with developers and other technical disciplines.

Experience with Infrastructure as Code, such as Terraform or Ansible.
Experience with VMware, Hyper-V or other virtualization platforms.

Experience with Perforce in a game-development environment.
Experience with game development pipelines and production environments.
Professional experience with Python, Go or another programming language.
Experience working in a game studio or other content-heavy development environment.
